summary:
A Man A Plan A Canal - Panama
The Panama Canal has become one of the integral waterways for world maritime commerce. Since the Canal opened for transit in 1914 it has facilitated the transportation of more than 200 million tons of cargo each year on over 14,000 ships. Although discussed for many years, in April a proposal indicated Panama's plans to expand the Canal to accommodate more traffic and larger vessels came together.

children.title: Suezmaxes Through Panama!
children.summary: Currently, the Canal is comprised of three sets of locks, each with two lanes. The Gatun Locks are on the on the Atlantic side and both the Pedro Miguel Locks and the Miraflores Locks on the Pacific side.

children.title: Why Expand?
children.summary: According to the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) some of the objectives of the expansion are to maintain the Canal's competitiveness as a viable maritime route and increase Canal payments to the National Treasury. The payments to the National Treasury are derived in three ways: on a per net ton basis, as a payment for public services and as a payment based on Canal operations.
